JIEJIE.NET_2026-01-01_dotnet8_cil_consol.build_flags: dotnet build JIEJIENETForCore.Console.csproj -c Debug (upstream's configuration: DefineConstants TRACE;DOTNETCORE, AllowUnsafeBlocks, Optimize=false), netcoreapp3.1, -p:ContinuousIntegrationBuild=true -p:PathMap=<checkout>=/_/
JIEJIE.NET_2026-01-01_dotnet8_cil_consol.notes: The obfuscator's own code, not its output. FortiGuard Labs (2026-08-04) says the generation-2 FDMTP loader Microsoft.ServiceHosting.Tools.dll in the QuickFox supply-chain attack 'is obfuscated using the JieJie .NET Protector tool'; that sentence is the only evidence, no code comparison is shown, and nothing here was checked against that sample. A protected assembly does not contain this engine, so this family recognises JIEJIE.NET itself. 59 of the 858 methods are namespace __DC20211119 (JIEJIEHelper, JIEJIEPerformanceCounter), the C# source of the helpers the tool injects into protected assemblies as IL text; whether they match the injected copies was not measured. Upstream's committed binaries are Debug builds, so both configurations are built. Pinned to f28e1d2, the last commit touching source/; the version the attackers used is unknown. The .NET Framework projects are not built: the console project file is committed E-SafeNet-encrypted and the GUI needs full-Framework MSBuild.
